verses.zh: 一到早晨，祭司长和长老、文士、全公会的人大家商议，就把耶稣捆绑，解去交给彼拉多。
verses.en: Early in the morning, after forming a plan, the chief priests with the elders and the experts in the law[NOTE:1] and the whole Sanhedrin tied Jesus up, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “and the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 1:22.

The Jews most assuredly wanted to put Jesus to death, but they lacked the authority to do so. For this reason they handed him over to Pilate in hopes of securing a death sentence. The Romans kept close control of the death penalty in conquered territories to prevent it being used to execute Roman sympathizers.

verses.zh: 彼拉多问他说：「你是犹太人的王吗？」耶稣回答说：「你说的是。」
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] Pilate asked him, “Are you the king[NOTE:2] of the Jews?” He replied,[NOTE:3] “You say so.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the implied result of previous action in the narrative.
“Are you the king of the Jews?” Pilate was interested in this charge because of its political implications of sedition against Rome.
Grk “answering, he said to him.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant, but the syntax of the phrase has been modified for clarity.
The reply “You say so” is somewhat enigmatic, like Jesus’ earlier reply to the Jewish leadership (mentioned in Matt 26:64 and Luke 22:70).

verses.zh: 祭司长告他许多的事。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] the chief priests began to accuse him repeatedly.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

verses.zh: 彼拉多又问他说：「你看，他们告你这么多的事，你甚么都不回答吗？」
verses.en: So Pilate asked him again,[NOTE:1] “Have you nothing to say? See how many charges they are bringing against you!”
notes: Grk “Pilate asked him again, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 耶稣仍不回答，以致彼拉多觉得希奇。
verses.en: But Jesus made no further reply, so that Pilate was amazed.

verses.zh: 每逢这节期，巡抚照众人所求的，释放一个囚犯给他们。
verses.en: During the feast it was customary to release one prisoner to the people,[NOTE:1] whomever they requested.
notes: Grk “them”; the referent (the people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.sn The custom of Pilate to release one prisoner to them is unknown outside the gospels in Jewish writings, but it was a Roman custom at the time and thus probably used in Palestine as well (cf. Matt 27:15; John 18:39); see W. W. Wessel, “Mark,” EBC 8:773-74.

verses.zh: 有一个人名叫巴拉巴，和作乱的人一同捆绑。他们做乱的时候，曾杀过人。
verses.en: A man named Barabbas was imprisoned with rebels who had committed murder during an insurrection.

verses.zh: 众人上去求巡抚，照常例给他们办。
verses.en: Then the crowd came up and began to ask Pilate to release a prisoner for them, as was his custom.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “Coming up the crowd began to ask [him to do] as he was doing for them.”

verses.zh: 彼拉多说：「你们要我释放犹太人的王给你们吗？」
verses.en: So Pilate asked them,[NOTE:1] “Do you want me to release the king of the Jews for you?”
notes: Grk “Pilate answered them, saying.” The participle λέγων (legōn) is redundant and has not been translated.

verses.zh: 他原晓得，祭司长是因为嫉妒才把耶稣解了来。
verses.en: (For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over because of envy.)[NOTE:1]
notes: This is a parenthetical note by the author.

verses.zh: 只是祭司长挑唆众人，宁可释放巴拉巴给他们。
verses.en: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release[NOTE:1] Barabbas instead.
notes: Grk “to have him release for them.”

verses.zh: 彼拉多又说：「那么样，你们所称为犹太人的王，我怎么办他呢？」
verses.en: So Pilate spoke to them again,[NOTE:1] “Then what do you want me to do[NOTE:2] with the one you call king of the Jews?”
notes: Grk “answering, Pilate spoke to them again.” The participle ἀποκριθείς (apokritheis) is redundant and has not been translated.

Instead of “what do you want me to do” several witnesses, including the most significant ones (א B C W Δ Ψ ƒ1,13 33 892), lack θέλετε (thelete, “you want”), turning the question into the more abrupt “what should I do?” Although the witnesses for the longer reading are not as significant (A D Θ 0250 M latt sy), the reading without θέλετε conforms to Matt 27:22 and thus is suspected of being a scribal emendation. The known scribal tendency to assimilate one synoptic passage to another parallel, coupled with the lack of such assimilation in mss that are otherwise known to do this most frequently (the Western and Byzantine texts), suggests that θέλετε is authentic. Further, Mark’s known style of being generally more verbose and redundant than Matthew’s argues that θέλετε is authentic here. That this is the longer reading, however, and that a good variety of witnesses omit the word, gives one pause. Perhaps the wording without θέλετε would have been perceived as having greater homiletical value, motivating scribes to move in this direction. A decision is difficult, but on the whole internal evidence leads toward regarding θέλετε as authentic.

verses.zh: 他们又喊着说：「把他钉十字架！」
verses.en: They shouted back, “Crucify[NOTE:1] him!”
notes: Crucifixion was the cruelest form of punishment practiced by the Romans. Roman citizens could not normally undergo it. It was reserved for the worst crimes, like treason and evasion of due process in a capital case. The Roman historian Cicero called it “a cruel and disgusting penalty” (Against Verres 2.5.63-66 §§163-70); Josephus (J. W. 7.6.4 [7.203]) called it the worst of deaths.

verses.zh: 彼拉多说：「为甚么呢？他做了甚么恶事呢？」他们便极力地喊着说：「把他钉十字架！」
verses.en: Pilate asked them, “Why? What has he done wrong?” But they shouted more insistently, “Crucify him!”

verses.zh: 彼拉多要叫众人喜悦，就释放巴拉巴给他们，将耶稣鞭打了，交给人钉十字架。
verses.en: Because he wanted to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas for them. Then,[NOTE:1] after he had Jesus flogged,[NOTE:2] he handed him over[NOTE:3] to be crucified.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.

A Roman flogging (traditionally, “scourging”) was an excruciating punishment. The victim was stripped of his clothes and bound to a post with his hands fastened above him (or sometimes he was thrown to the ground). Guards standing on either side of the victim would incessantly beat him with a whip (flagellum) made out of leather with pieces of lead and bone inserted into its ends. While the Jews only allowed 39 lashes, the Romans had no such limit; many people who received such a beating died as a result. See C. Schneider, TDNT, 4:515-19. tn The Greek term φραγελλόω (phragelloō) refers to flogging. BDAG 1064 s.v. states, “flog, scourge, a punishment inflicted on slaves and provincials after a sentence of death had been pronounced on them. So in the case of Jesus before the crucifixion…Mt 27:26; Mk 15:15.”
Or “delivered him up.”

verses.zh: 兵丁把耶稣带进衙门院里，叫齐了全营的兵。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] the soldiers led him into the palace (that is, the governor’s residence)[NOTE:2] and called together the whole cohort.[NOTE:3]
notes: Here δέ (de) has been translated as “So” to indicate that the soldiers’ action is in response to Pilate’s condemnation of the prisoner in v. 15.

Grk “(that is, the praetorium).” sn The governor’s residence (Grk “praetorium”) was the Roman governor’s official residence. The one in Jerusalem may have been Herod’s palace in the western part of the city, or the fortress Antonia northwest of the temple area.
A Roman cohort was a tenth of a legion, about 500-600 soldiers.

verses.zh: 他们给他穿上紫袍，又用荆棘编做冠冕给他戴上，
verses.en: They put a purple cloak[NOTE:1] on him and after braiding[NOTE:2] a crown of thorns,[NOTE:3] they put it on him.
notes: The purple cloak probably refers to a military garment which had the color of royal purple, and thus resembled a king’s robe. The soldiers did this to Jesus as a form of mockery in view of the charges that he was a king (cf. 15:2).
Or “weaving.”

The crown may have been made from palm spines or some other thorny plant common in Israel. In placing the crown of thorns on his head, the soldiers were unwittingly symbolizing God’s curse on humanity (cf. Gen 3:18) being placed on Jesus. Their purpose would have been to mock Jesus’ claim to be a king; the crown of thorns would have represented the “radiant corona” portrayed on the heads of rulers on coins and other artifacts in the 1st century.

verses.zh: 就庆贺他说：「恭喜，犹太人的王啊！」
verses.en: They began to salute him: “Hail, king of the Jews!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “Long live the King of the Jews!”sn The statement Hail, King of the Jews! is a mockery patterned after the Romans’ cry of Ave, Caesar (“Hail, Caesar!”).

verses.zh: 又拿一根苇子打他的头，吐唾沫在他脸上，屈膝拜他。
verses.en: Again and again[NOTE:1] they struck him on the head with a staff[NOTE:2] and spit on him. Then they knelt down and paid homage to him.
notes: The verb here has been translated as an iterative imperfect.
Or “a reed.” The Greek term can mean either “staff” or “reed.” See BDAG 502 s.v. κάλαμος 2.

verses.zh: 戏弄完了，就给他脱了紫袍，仍穿上他自己的衣服，带他出去，要钉十字架。
verses.en: When they had finished mocking[NOTE:1] him, they stripped him of the purple cloak and put his own clothes back on him. Then[NOTE:2] they led him away to crucify him.[NOTE:3]
notes: The aorist tense is taken consummatively here.
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
See the note on Crucify in 15:13.

verses.zh: 有一个古利奈人西门，就是亚历山大和鲁孚的父亲，从乡下来，经过那地方，他们就勉强他同去，好背着耶稣的十字架。
verses.en: The soldiers[NOTE:1] forced[NOTE:2] a passerby to carry his cross,[NOTE:3] Simon of Cyrene, who was coming in from the country[NOTE:4] (he was the father of Alexander and Rufus).
notes: Grk “They”; the referent (the soldiers) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “conscripted”; or “pressed into service.”

Jesus was beaten severely with a whip before this (the prelude to crucifixion, known to the Romans as verberatio, mentioned in Matt 27:26; Mark 15:15; John 19:1), so he would have been weak from trauma and loss of blood. Apparently he was unable to bear the cross himself, so Simon was conscripted to help (in all probability this was only the crossbeam, called in Latin the patibulum, since the upright beam usually remained in the ground at the place of execution). Cyrene was located in North Africa where Tripoli is today. Nothing more is known about this Simon.
Or perhaps, “was coming in from his field” outside the city (BDAG 15-16 s.v. ἀγρός 1).

verses.zh: 他们带耶稣到了各各他地方（各各他翻出来就是髑髅地），
verses.en: They brought Jesus[NOTE:1] to a place called Golgotha[NOTE:2] (which is translated, “Place of the Skull”).[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “him.”
Grk “a place, Golgotha.” This is an Aramaic name; see John 19:17.

The place called Golgotha (which is translated “Place of the Skull”). This location is north and just outside of Jerusalem. The hill on which it is located protruded much like a skull, giving the place its name. The Latin word for the Greek term κρανίον (kranion) is calvaria, from which the English word “Calvary” is derived (cf. Luke 23:33 in the KJV).

verses.zh: 拿没药调和的酒给耶稣，他却不受。
verses.en: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh,[NOTE:1] but he did not take it.
notes: It is difficult to say for certain who gave Jesus this drink of wine mixed with myrrh (e.g., the executioner, or perhaps women from Jerusalem). In any case, whoever gave it to him most likely did so in order to relieve his pain, but Jesus was unwilling to take it.

verses.zh: 于是将他钉在十字架上，拈阄分他的衣服，看是谁得甚么。
verses.en: Then[NOTE:1] they crucified[NOTE:2] him and divided his clothes, throwing dice[NOTE:3] for them, to decide what each would take.
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
See the note on Crucify in 15:13.

Grk “by throwing the lot” (probably by using marked pebbles or broken pieces of pottery). A modern equivalent, “throwing dice,” was chosen here because of its association with gambling. According to L&N 6.219 a term for “dice” is particularly appropriate.sn An allusion to Ps 22:18.

verses.zh: 钉他在十字架上是巳初的时候。
verses.en: It was nine o’clock in the morning[NOTE:1] when they crucified him.
notes: Grk “It was the third hour.” This time would have been approximate, and could refer to the beginning of the process, some time before Jesus was lifted on the cross.

verses.zh: 在上面有他的罪状，写的是：「犹太人的王。」
verses.en: The inscription[NOTE:1] of the charge against him read, “The king of the Jews.”
notes: Mention of the inscription is an important detail because the inscription would normally give the reason for the execution. It shows that Jesus was executed for claiming to be a king. It was also probably written with irony from the executioners’ point of view.

verses.zh: 他们又把两个强盗和他同钉十字架，一个在右边，一个在左边。（有古卷加：
verses.en: And they crucified two outlaws with him, one on his right and one on his left.[NOTE:1]
notes: Most later mss add 15:28 “And the scripture was fulfilled that says, ‘He was counted with the lawless ones.’” Verse 28 is included in L Θ 083 0250 ƒ1,13 33 M lat, but is lacking in significant Alexandrian and Western mss and some others (א A B C D Ψ). The addition of the verse with its quotation from Isa 53:12 probably represents a scribal assimilation from Luke 22:37. It was almost certainly not an original part of Mark’s Gospel. The present translation follows NA28 in omitting the verse number, a procedure also followed by a number of other modern translations.

verses.zh: 这就应了经上的话说：他被列在罪犯之中。）
从那里经过的人辱骂他，摇着头说：「咳！你这拆毁圣殿、三日又建造起来的，
verses.en: Those who passed by defamed him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who can destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,

verses.zh: 可以救自己，从十字架上下来吧！」
verses.en: save yourself and come down from the cross!”[NOTE:1]
notes: There is rich irony in the statement of those who were passing by, “Save yourself and come down from the cross!” In summary, they wanted Jesus to come down from the cross and save his physical life, but it was indeed his staying on the cross and giving his physical life that led to the fact that they could experience a resurrection from death to life. There is a similar kind of irony in the statement made by the chief priests and experts in the law in 15:31.

verses.zh: 祭司长和文士也是这样戏弄他，彼此说：「他救了别人，不能救自己。
verses.en: In the same way even the chief priests—together with the experts in the law[NOTE:1]—were mocking him among themselves:[NOTE:2] “He saved others, but he cannot save himself!
notes: Or “with the scribes.” See the note on the phrase “experts in the law” in 1:22. Only “chief priests” is in the nominative case; this sentence structure attempts to capture this emphasis.
Grk “Mocking him, the chief priests…said among themselves.”

verses.zh: 以色列的王基督，现在可以从十字架上下来，叫我们看见，就信了。」那和他同钉的人也是讥诮他。
verses.en: Let the Christ,[NOTE:1] the king of Israel, come down from the cross now, that we may see and believe!” Those who were crucified with him also spoke abusively to him.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “the Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”sn See the note on Christ in 8:29.
Mark’s wording suggests that both of the criminals spoke abusively to him. If so, one of them quickly changed his attitude toward Jesus (see Luke 23:40-43).

verses.zh: 从午正到申初，遍地都黑暗了。
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when it was noon,[NOTE:2] darkness came over the whole land[NOTE:3] until three in the afternoon.[NOTE:4]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic.
Grk “When the sixth hour had come.”
This imagery has parallels to the Day of the Lord: Joel 2:10; Amos 8:9; Zeph 1:15.
Grk “until the ninth hour.”

verses.zh: 申初的时候，耶稣大声喊着说：「以罗伊！以罗伊！拉马撒巴各大尼？」（翻出来就是：我的　神！我的　神！为甚么离弃我？）
verses.en: Around three o’clock[NOTE:1] Jesus cried out with a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”[NOTE:2]
notes: The repetition of the phrase “three o’clock” preserves the author’s rougher, less elegant style (cf. Matt 27:45-46; Luke 23:44). Although such stylistic matters are frequently handled differently in the translation because the issue of synoptic literary dependence is involved here, it was considered important to reflect some of the stylistic differences among the synoptics in the translation, so that the English reader can be aware of them.
A quotation from Ps 22:1.

verses.zh: 旁边站着的人，有的听见就说：「看哪，他叫以利亚呢！」
verses.en: When some of the bystanders heard it they said, “Listen, he is calling for Elijah!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Perhaps the crowd thought Jesus was calling for Elijah because the exclamation “my God, my God” (i.e., in Aramaic, Eloi, Eloi) sounds like the name Elijah.

verses.zh: 有一个人跑去，把海绒蘸满了醋，绑在苇子上，送给他喝，说：「且等着，看以利亚来不来把他取下。」
verses.en: Then someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine,[NOTE:1] put it on a stick,[NOTE:2] and gave it to him to drink, saying, “Leave him alone! Let’s see if Elijah will come to take him down!”
notes: Sour wine refers to cheap wine that was called in Latin posca, a cheap vinegar wine diluted heavily with water. It was the drink of slaves and soldiers, and was probably there for the soldiers who had performed the crucifixion.
Grk “a reed.”

verses.zh: 耶稣大声喊叫，气就断了。
verses.en: But Jesus cried out with a loud voice and breathed his last.

verses.zh: 殿里的幔子从上到下裂为两半。
verses.en: And the temple curtain[NOTE:1] was torn in two, from top to bottom.
notes: The referent of this term, καταπέτασμα (katapetasma), is not entirely clear. It could refer to the curtain separating the holy of holies from the holy place (Josephus, J. W. 5.5.5 [5.219]), or it could refer to one at the entrance of the temple court (Josephus, J. W. 5.5.4 [5.212]). Many argue that the inner curtain is meant because another term, κάλυμμα (kalumma), is also used for the outer curtain. Others see a reference to the outer curtain as more likely because of the public nature of this sign. Either way, the symbolism means that access to God has been opened up. It also pictures a judgment that includes the sacrifices.

verses.zh: 对面站着的百夫长看见耶稣这样喊叫（有古卷没有喊叫二字）断气，就说：「这人真是　神的儿子！」
verses.en: Now when the centurion,[NOTE:1] who stood in front of him, saw how he died,[NOTE:2] he said, “Truly this man was God’s Son!”
notes: A centurion was a noncommissioned officer in the Roman army or one of the auxiliary territorial armies, commanding a centuria of (nominally) 100 men. The responsibilities of centurions were broadly similar to modern junior officers, but there was a wide gap in social status between them and officers, and relatively few were promoted beyond the rank of senior centurion. The Roman troops stationed in Judea were auxiliaries, who would normally be rewarded with Roman citizenship after 25 years of service. Some of the centurions throughout the region may have served originally in the Roman legions (regular army) and thus gained their citizenship at enlistment. Others may have inherited it, like the apostle Paul did (cf. Acts 22:28).
Grk “the way he breathed his last”; or “the way he expired”; or “that he thus breathed no more.”

verses.zh: 还有些妇女远远地观看；内中有抹大拉的马利亚，又有小雅各和约西的母亲马利亚，并有撒罗米，
verses.en: There were also women, watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses,[NOTE:1] and Salome.
notes: In Matt 27:56 the name Joses is written as Joseph.

verses.zh: 就是耶稣在加利利的时候，跟随他、服事他的那些人，还有同耶稣上耶路撒冷的好些妇女在那里观看。
verses.en: When he was in Galilee, they had followed him and given him support.[NOTE:1] Many other women who had come up with him to Jerusalem[NOTE:2] were there too.
notes: Cf. Luke 8:3.tn Grk “and ministered to him.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 到了晚上，因为这是预备日，就是安息日的前一日，
verses.en: Now[NOTE:1] when evening had already come, since it was the day of preparation (that is, the day before the Sabbath),[NOTE:2]
notes: Here καί (kai) has been translated as “now” to indicate the transition to a new topic and introduction of a new character.
The day of preparation was the day before the Sabbath when everything had to be prepared for it, as no work could be done on the Sabbath.

verses.zh: 有亚利马太的约瑟前来，他是尊贵的议士，也是等候　神国的。他放胆进去见彼拉多，求耶稣的身体；
verses.en: Joseph of Arimathea, a highly regarded member of the council,[NOTE:1] who was himself looking forward to[NOTE:2] the kingdom of God,[NOTE:3] went boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “a councillor” (as a member of the Sanhedrin, see L&N 11.85). This indicates that some individuals among the leaders did respond to Jesus.

Or “waiting for.”sn Though some dispute that Joseph of Arimathea was a disciple of Jesus, this remark that he was looking forward to the kingdom of God and his actions regarding Jesus’ burial suggest otherwise.

The kingdom of God is a major theme of Jesus’ teaching. The nature of the kingdom of God in the NT and in Jesus’ teaching has long been debated by interpreters and scholars, with discussion primarily centering around the nature of the kingdom (earthly, heavenly, or both) and the kingdom’s arrival (present, future, or both). An additional major issue concerns the relationship between the kingdom of God and the person and work of Jesus himself.

Asking for the body of Jesus was indeed a bold move on the part of Joseph of Arimathea, for it clearly and openly identified him with a man who had just been condemned and executed, namely, Jesus. His faith is exemplary, especially for someone who was a member of the council that handed Jesus over for crucifixion (cf. Luke 23:51). He did this because he sought to give Jesus an honorable burial.

verses.zh: 彼拉多诧异耶稣已经死了，便叫百夫长来，问他耶稣死了久不久。
verses.en: Pilate was surprised that he was already dead. He[NOTE:1] called the centurion[NOTE:2] and asked him if he had been dead for some time.
notes: Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, a new sentence was started here in the translation.
See the note on the word centurion in 15:39.

verses.zh: 既从百夫长得知实情，就把耶稣的尸首赐给约瑟。
verses.en: When Pilate[NOTE:1] was informed by the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Pilate) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 约瑟买了细麻布，把耶稣取下来，用细麻布裹好，安放在磐石中凿出来的坟墓里，又滚过一块石头来挡住墓门。
verses.en: After Joseph[NOTE:1] bought a linen cloth[NOTE:2] and took down the body, he wrapped it in the linen and placed it in a tomb cut out of the rock.[NOTE:3] Then[NOTE:4] he rolled a stone across the entrance[NOTE:5] of the tomb.
notes: Grk “he”; the referent (Joseph of Arimathea) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
The term σινδών (sindōn) can refer to a linen cloth used either for clothing or for burial.
That is, cut or carved into an outcropping of natural rock, resulting in a cave-like structure (see L&N 19.25).
Here καί (kai) has been translated as “then” to indicate the implied sequence of events within the narrative.
Or “to the door,” “against the door.”

verses.zh: 抹大拉的马利亚和约西的母亲马利亚都看见安放他的地方。
verses.en: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses saw where the body[NOTE:1] was placed.
notes: Grk “it”; the referent (Jesus’ body) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
